items.followUp: What is the difference between volatile and non-volatile memory?

rubric.why: Identifies that non-volatile memory retains its contents when power is off.
rubric.description: States that non-volatile memory keeps data without power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this defining property.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates understanding of the type of memory.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of non-volatile memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for at least one valid example.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the computer’s power is switched off.
Examples include ROM and flash memory.

items.followUp: How are letters and numbers represented inside a digital computer?

rubric.why: Digital computers represent data using the binary system.
rubric.description: Names binary as the system used to store data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying binary representation.

rubric.why: Binary data is made up of the two digits 0 and 1.
rubric.description: States that data is stored as combinations of 0s and 1s.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both binary digits or explaining their use.

modelAnswer: Digital computers store data in binary form.
All data is represented by combinations of the digits 0 and 1, called bits.

items.followUp: Draw the truth table for P OR Q OR NOT Q.

rubric.why: The NOT P column must be the complement of P for each input row.
rubric.description: Gives the correct values for NOT P in the truth table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct NOT P column.

rubric.why: P OR Q OR NOT P is true for every possible pair of inputs.
rubric.description: Gives the correct final column, which is true in all four rows.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct final column.

modelAnswer: Here, + means OR, and NOT P is the complement of P.
| P | Q | NOT P | P + Q + NOT P |

items.followUp: State the commutative law for the AND operation.

rubric.why: The law is defined by the fact that changing operand order leaves the result unchanged.
rubric.description: Explains that changing the order of operands does not change the result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining statement.

rubric.why: A valid equation demonstrates the commutative property.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example using OR or AND.

modelAnswer: The commutative law states that changing the order of operands does not change the result.
For example, A + B = B + A (OR) and A × B = B × A (AND).

items.followUp: Write the truth table for the logical operators AND, OR and NOT.

rubric.why: AND and OR are two of the basic logical operators.
NOT is the third basic logical operator.

modelAnswer: The basic logical operators are AND, OR and NOT.

items.followUp: What is a graphical user interface (GUI)?

rubric.why: A client user interface is the part of a system presented to the client or user.
rubric.description: Identifies it as the interface or front end presented to the client.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the interface.

rubric.why: The interface lets the client use the application or communicate with a server.
rubric.description: States that the user interacts with the application through it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its function.

modelAnswer: A client user interface is the front end displayed on the client device.
It allows the user to interact with an application and send requests to the server.

items.followUp: What is the main difference between a hub and a switch?

rubric.why: Both hubs and switches connect devices on a network.
rubric.description: States that it connects computers or devices on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the shared function.

rubric.why: Describing how either device handles data distinguishes a valid definition.
rubric.description: Explains that a hub broadcasts to all ports or a switch forwards data to its destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of either device.

modelAnswer: A hub or switch is a networking device used to connect computers or other devices in a LAN.
A hub sends received data to all its ports, whereas a switch forwards data to the intended device.

items.followUp: Name any four layers of the OSI network model.

rubric.why: Any two distinct layers from a recognized layered network model satisfy the question.
rubric.description: Names any two valid layers in a layered network model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each valid, distinct layer name.

modelAnswer: Two layers of the OSI network model are the Physical layer and the Network layer.
